nodes.text: could a boy have carried five pounds of silver!
Every morning you tell me nothing but dreams about me,
to stir my mind and make it anxious.
Already last year’s vintage, and this one too, has come down to the dregs,
while a wise woman expiates your nights for me;
I have used up salted meal and heaps of incense;
my flocks have dwindled, as lamb after lamb falls;
not a pig, not a farmyard bird, not an egg is left.
Either stay awake, Nasidianus, or sleep for yourself.
If you send gifts back to no one, Chrestus,
nor the Jew taught by his mother to beg,
nor the bleary-eyed pedlar of sulphured wares.
Who can count the losses of lazy sleep?
He will tell how many bronzes the city’s hands beat
when the Moon, cut by the Colchian *rhombus* [magic wheel], is beaten.
You, Sparsus, know nothing of these things, nor can you know,
living in luxury on your Petilian domain,
